intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county, city, and school district and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Clark County's governments, from the reports in our document library — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' In those reports, the phrase signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: No material weaknesses in internal control were identified. Federal grant compliance is audited separately and that report had not yet been issued.

Machine reading of both reports surfaced no findings, deficiency, or noncompliance language beyond standard definitions. These older-format reports are queued for a page-by-page visual pass before we call them clean outright.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: No material weaknesses in internal control were identified in either year.
No material weaknesses in internal control were identified; the compliance report follows the standard no-findings form.

verdicts.quote: No significant deficiencies or material weaknesses were disclosed during the audit of the financial statements. No instances of noncompliance material to the financial statements of the System were disclosed by the audit.

verdicts.detail: Both the financial statement findings and the federal award findings sections. Unmodified (clean) opinion on federal program compliance; the district qualified as a low-risk auditee.
No material weaknesses, no reportable findings, unmodified opinion on federal compliance, and no prior-year findings carried forward.

limits: Audits test whether the books follow the rules and whether controls work. They do not evaluate spending choices, pay levels, or economic-development incentives.
A clean audit and records that are not posted online can both be true: an audit tests whether the books follow the rules, not what the county publishes.
The FY2024 county audit is not yet published; this page updates when it is.
minutes_finding: First OCR result from the archived minutes (December 8, 2025 regular session): Ordinance 2025-21 — the 2026 budget this whole site navigates — was adopted unanimously, all eleven justices voting Yea by name. The same meeting adopted the 2026 property tax levy (Ordinance 2025-19) and Ordinance 2025-22, 'amending and adopting a base pay threshold for all new full-time county employees beginning January 1, 2026'. Obtaining 2025-22's text is now on the docket.
